account.conflictBody: The account is at revision {rev} and this browser has changes too. Pick which copy wins — nothing is overwritten until you do.
account.lockedHelp: This device is signed in but has no encryption key — enter your password to unlock it.
account.migrateBody: This browser has data and your new account has none. Upload it so your phone and desktop see the same dashboard?
account.passphraseHint: Use a memorable passphrase of at least 15 characters. It protects both sign-in and encrypted data if the database is stolen.
account.privacyIntro: Your readings are encrypted in this browser before they are uploaded. The server stores a blob it cannot open — it knows
account.privacyRest: it changed, not what is in it, and not your password.
account.pushUnconfigured: This server has no VAPID keys yet, so notifications cannot be delivered.
account.recoverWarn: The stored copy was encrypted with the old password and will be removed — this recovers your account, not your data. Re-sync from a device that still has it.
account.recoveryBody: Keep this recovery code for local compatibility mode only. For public accounts, password recovery uses a one-time e-mail link; the stored copy remains encrypted with the old password.
account.recoveryLinkHelp: Open the e-mail link to choose a new password. The link proves mailbox control and is used only once.
account.recoveryRequest: If that mailbox can receive mail, a recovery link is on its way. Open it to choose a new password.
account.registrationClosed: Registration is closed until mailbox verification and the concrete retention policy are configured. You will choose a passphrase only after proving control of your email address.

accrual.billDateBillingDay: Bill date {day} = your billing-day setting (no bills in this file).
accrual.billDateCadence: Bill date {day} = your last bill's read date + its median length.
accrual.billDateNewest: Chart stops at {day}, the newest day you have readings for.
accrual.commodityOnlyNote: Commodity (variable) charges only — no delivery, regulatory charges or HST.
accrual.emptyNote: No open billing period to accrue against yet.
accrual.explainer: Grey line = spent so far this period (your estimate). Yellow dashed = where you’re on pace to land by the bill date. Dotted = your average of the last 3 bills.
accrual.noBillsYet: no bills to compare against yet
accrual.notStartedNote: The open period starts after your newest reading — nothing has accrued yet.
accrual.paceNone: Not enough readings yet to draw a pace line.
accrual.paceProjection: Pace = your last {days}-day average of {daily}/day (Wave F's projection math), carried across all {period} days of this period.
accrual.paceRunRate: Pace = this period's own run-rate of {daily}/day — no projection is available yet.
accrual.tierCross: Tier 1's {kwh} kWh runs out {day} — everything after bills at the tier-2 rate, which this line does not include.
accrual.tierCrossPace: Tier 1's {kwh} kWh runs out {day} at this pace — everything after bills at the tier-2 rate, which this line does not include.
actualBill.blurb: Every line item the utility billed, next to what this app estimates for the same period. Line names are shown in your language; hover one for the utility’s own wording. Nothing here is retyped or fetched — it is all in the file you imported.
actualBill.checkOffA: Our rate assumptions are off — for this period our rates estimate
actualBill.checkOffAdvice: Check the prices and fees on your utility bill before relying on this estimate.
actualBill.commoditySkip: Not compared — this bill states no charge lines, so there is no commodity figure for our rates to land on.
actualBill.coverage: your readings cover {covered} of {days} days ({pct}, {needed} needed).
actualBill.crosscheck: Billed {billed} · your readings add up to {metered} (Δ {delta}).
actualBill.deliveryFit: ≈ {flat} fixed per period + {cents}/kWh — fitted across {periods} periods, ±{residual}
actualBill.noChargeLines: no charge lines in this bill
actualBill.noReadings: this browser holds no readings inside this period.
actualBill.pctOfSubtotalScales: {pct} of the subtotal — scales with it

actualBill.straightFromXml_one: Straight from your XML · 1 billing period
actualBill.straightFromXml_other: Straight from your XML · {count} billing periods
actualBill.title: Your actual bill
alerts.deniedMsg: The browser did not grant permission — the in-app banner still works.
alerts.granted: On. You will get an alert here when the best plan or the rates change.
alerts.onDeviceOnly: There is no account, so nothing here can email or text you: alerts are on-device only, and stop entirely if this browser clears its site data.
alerts.permBlocked: Blocked — allow notifications for this site in your browser settings.
alerts.permOff: Off — turn on to get an alert when the tab is closed.

alerts.permUnsupported: Not available — this browser exposes no notification API here.

alerts.syncUnsupported: Periodic background sync: not in this browser (Chromium-only, installed app only). Refreshing on tab focus instead.
alerts.title: Alerts
alerts.turnedOff: Turned off. The browser permission stays granted — this app just goes quiet.
alerts.watchesTwo: Live sync watches two things after every refresh: the best of your three plans, and whether new Ontario rates are in effect. When either changes you get the banner at the top of the dashboard.

backup.errBadJson: That file is not valid JSON ({reason}). Choose a file produced by “Export JSON”.
backup.errBadVersion: That backup has a missing or invalid "version" (got {got}).
backup.errBillingDay: That backup has an invalid billing_day (got {got}, expected an integer 1–31).
backup.errEmpty: That file is empty. Choose a file produced by “Export JSON”.
backup.errEnergyNotArray: That backup's energy_data is not an array (got {got}).
backup.errExampleFlag: That backup has an invalid energy_data_is_example (got {got}, expected true or false).
backup.errGasClock: That backup's gas_local_time_parameters is not a clock this build can read (got {got}).
backup.errGasShape: That backup's gas_data section is not a valid gas dataset (got {got}).
backup.errGasSummaries: That backup's gas_usage_summaries is not an array of billing periods (got {got}).
backup.errGasSummaryEntry: That backup's gas_usage_summaries entry {n} is not a billing period this build can read (got {got}).
backup.errNewer: This backup was created by a newer version of the app (schema v{version}; this build understands up to v{max}). Update the app, then try the import again.
backup.errNoGasReadings: That backup's gas section contains no readings — a backup never carries an empty dataset.
backup.errNoPayload: That backup has no "payload" object — nothing to restore.
backup.errNoReadings: That backup contains no readings — restoring it would wipe your data.
backup.errNoSchema: That file has no "schema" marker, so it is not an energy-dashboard backup. Expected "{expected}".
backup.errNotBackup: That file is not an energy-dashboard backup (expected a JSON object).
backup.errPlanEntry: That backup's plan_timeline entry {n} is invalid — each entry needs an id, a plan (TOU, Tiered or ULO) and from/to days in yyyy-MM-dd with from on or before to (got {got}).
backup.errPlanTimeline: That backup has an invalid plan_timeline (got {got}, expected an array of {id, plan, from, to}).
backup.errReadJson: Could not read {name}. Choose the JSON file produced by “Export JSON”.
backup.errRefused: This browser refused to save the readings ({detail}). Nothing was changed.
backup.errRefusedBackup: This browser refused to save the backup (storage may be full or blocked). Nothing was changed.
backup.errRefusedBillingDay: This browser refused to save the billing day ({detail}). Nothing was changed.
backup.errRowNotReading: Row {n} of the backup is not a reading object (got {got}).
backup.errSelectedPlan: That backup has an invalid selected_plan ({got}), expected one of {plans}.
backup.errUnsupportedSchema: That backup uses schema v{version}, which this build (v{max}) cannot restore.
backup.errWrongSchema: That file belongs to a different app: its schema is "{schema}", expected "{expected}".
backup.everything: Everything lives in this browser — no server copy. Export a JSON backup before clearing your profile, switching devices, or just to keep one.
backup.import.failDetail: The file was not recognised as an export of this app.

backup.import.failHintAtomic: Nothing was changed: an import is accepted whole or not at all.

backup.importFailed: That file could not be imported.

The line is real and large — it just is not a straight line of usage, so {blended}¢/kWh is the only rate that describes it honestly.

charge.headlineNoFixed: Of your {amount} {noun} this period, none of it is fixed — you would pay $0.00 at 0 kWh, and all {variable} is volume-driven.

delta.notBills: Columns marked with a badge are not bills: an estimate of what has not been billed yet, or days no bill in this file covers — no change is computed across them.
delta.noteBaseline: Only one billing period here — every number in it is the baseline, so there is nothing to compare against yet.
delta.noteEmpty: No billing periods in this file.

diag.budgetHeadline: This file is too large, too deeply nested or too repetitive to open.
diag.budgetHint1: Export a shorter date range from your utility portal — a year at a time imports comfortably.
diag.budgetHint2: If you did not download this file yourself, treat it as untrusted.
diag.emptyDetail: It contains no bytes at all.
diag.emptyHint: Download the export again from your utility portal and retry.
diag.entityDetail: The document contains a DOCTYPE with an <!ENTITY …> declaration. External entities are a known way to read files from the machine doing the parsing, so they are refused on purpose.
diag.entityHeadline: This file declares XML external entities, which are not accepted.
diag.entityHint1: Re-export the data from your utility portal — genuine Green Button files do not define entities.
diag.entityHint2: If this file came from somewhere else, treat it as untrusted and do not open it elsewhere either.
diag.entriesDetail: Each <entry> should contain an <IntervalBlock> with <IntervalReading> elements (the actual meter readings). None were present — the export carried only metadata (usage point, meter, or summary information).
diag.entriesHeadline_one: Found {count} entry, but no interval readings inside them.
diag.entriesHeadline_other: Found {count} entries, but no interval readings inside them.
diag.entriesHint1: Choose the export option that includes interval data (hourly or 15-minute readings).
diag.entriesHint2: If the portal offers “summary” and “interval/detail” exports, pick interval/detail.
diag.htmlDetail: The file starts with HTML. Portals often hand back a login or error page when the download link expires — the Green Button export itself was never saved.
diag.htmlHeadline: That looks like a web page, not an export.
diag.htmlHint1: Sign in to your utility portal again and use the Green Button / “Download My Data” export action.
diag.htmlHint2: The file you want is usually named *.xml and starts with “<?xml” or “<feed”.
diag.malformedDetail: The file ended before its tags were balanced.
diag.malformedDetailAttr: An attribute is repeated, written without quotes, or given no value.
diag.malformedDetailChar: A character sits where XML allows none — usually an unescaped &, a stray <, or a control character.
diag.malformedDetailTag: A tag in it is opened and never closed, or closed by the wrong tag.
diag.malformedHeadlineLine: The XML is not well-formed at line {line}.
diag.malformedHint1: Downloads sometimes get truncated — re-download the export and try again.
diag.malformedHint2: If you edited the file by hand, restore the original.
diag.noDataDetail: The XML is readable, but it has no <entry> sections and no <IntervalReading> elements — there is no meter data in it.
diag.noDataHeadline: No Green Button data found in this file.
diag.noDataHint1: Make sure you exported “Green Button Download My Data” (XML), not a bill, summary or usage chart.
diag.noDataHint2: Some portals split the file by date range — export the full range and retry.
diag.noRowsDetail: The document has {count} entries and {readings} readings, but none of them yielded a usable timestamp/value pair.
diag.noRowsHeadline: This file looks like Green Button data but produced no readable rows.
diag.noRowsHint1: Try a different date range or a full export from your utility portal.
diag.noRowsHint2: If it keeps happening, re-download the file — this one may be truncated.
diag.noTimeDetail: Every <IntervalReading> needs a <timePeriod><start>…</start></timePeriod> holding a Unix timestamp. Without it a reading cannot be placed on the timeline, so nothing can be imported.
diag.noTimeHeadline_one: Found {count} reading, but none of them has a timestamp.
diag.noTimeHeadline_other: Found {count} readings, but none of them has a timestamp.
diag.noTimeHint1: Re-download the export — this one lost its time period block.
diag.noTimeHint2: If the file was edited or converted, use the original download.
diag.notXmlDetail: The file starts with “{head}…”, which is not the “<” an XML export begins with.
diag.notXmlHint1: Use the Green Button / “Download My Data” export from your utility portal (it produces an .xml file).
diag.notXmlHintJson: JSON exports are not supported — export XML.
diag.notXmlHintOther: CSV and PDF downloads are not supported.

efficiency.bandsNoteNone: Bands are Ontario’s rate seasons (Nov 1 – Apr 30 winter); red ticks are rate changes: none inside this data.
efficiency.caption: ¢ per kilowatt-hour · Total Electricity Charges ÷ billed kWh

efficiency.hstNote: HST on your bills is {pct}%; the incl.-tax figure adds that line back over the same kWh. Water and gas are billed separately and are never in these numbers.
efficiency.oneBill: One bill so far — the line starts at your second.
efficiency.splitNote: Usage prices YOUR commodity at today’s OEB rates; the rate line is what the schedule did instead. Delivery & fixed is the rest of the bill — no public rate schedule to reprice, so it is reported beside the verdict, never credited with it.
efficiency.subtitle: ALL electricity charges (commodity + delivery + regulatory) ÷ billed kWh — tax excluded

ev.againstMoving: against moving the same kWh to 23:00–07:00 on Ultra-Low Overnight.
ev.alreadyOptimal: Already in the overnight window — you're optimal at this hour, nothing to shift.
ev.alreadyOvernightDiff: You already charge {label}, inside 23:00–07:00 — nothing to shift. {stay} now on {plan} vs {move} on Ultra-Low Overnight: that {delta} is the plan, not the clock.
ev.alreadyOvernightSame: You already charge {label} — inside ULO's 23:00–07:00 window, at the cheapest rate those hours ever get: {stay} now, {move} after a switch. Nothing to gain by moving this charge.
ev.assumeBand: The stay side spreads your charge across {band} — the {hour}:00 you told us, plus one hour either side for habit drift — and prices each of those hours from your own readings ({seasons} rates, weekday and weekend windows as they fell).
ev.assumeBasisHour: priced it at the {hour}:00 you told us, not at the block we found
ev.assumeCommodityOnly: Rates are OEB commodity only — delivery, regulatory charges and HST are not in these numbers.
ev.assumeDetected: Charging window read from your own data: {label}, {detail}. We can only see a block of load — we cannot tell an EV apart from any other timed appliance.
ev.assumeDoubleCount: Stay vs move prices only your charging kWh — the SAME energy the three-plan comparison credits once, below. Two views of one credit: don't add them together.
ev.assumeNoBlockBound: No overnight charging block turned up in your data, so the plan comparison prices this energy as if it charges during your most expensive hours today. Treat the swing as an upper bound, not a measurement.
ev.assumeNoBlockHour: No overnight charging block turned up in your data — the hour you gave ({hour}:00) is the only evidence of when this charge happens.
ev.assumePeakExposure: {label} is ULO On-Peak at {rate}/kWh — the exposure flagged below.
ev.assumePerCharge: $ per charge assumes the whole charge lands in 23:00–07:00, the ULO overnight window.
ev.assumeStay: The stay side prices your charge where your own data puts it ({label}), read back from the readings' period charges.
ev.assumeTagged: You tagged {tagged} kWh a night; the overnight block in your data averages {actual} kWh/night ({label}). We priced YOUR number and {basis}.
ev.assumeWorstCase: No readings at {label}, so the "stay put" side prices your charge at your plan's most expensive rate — an upper bound, not a measurement.
ev.betterOff: Staying at {label} on {plan} costs {stay}. Moving the same charge to 23:00–07:00 on Ultra-Low Overnight costs {move} — {delta} better off every month.
ev.blurb: What a night's charge costs, and what your weekday 4–9pm window is worth at risk.
ev.detectedDetail: {kwh} kWh a night across {hours} h ({kw} kW average), seen on {nights} of {days} days
ev.exposureBasis_one: Commodity only — no delivery, regulatory charges or HST. And a run-rate, not a metered month: every /month here is this window scaled to 30.4 days from {days} day of your data.
ev.exposureBasis_other: Commodity only — no delivery, regulatory charges or HST. And a run-rate, not a metered month: every /month here is this window scaled to 30.4 days from {days} days of your data.
ev.headlineLead: A night's charge on ULO costs
ev.hourPrefilled: Charging hour prefilled from the block we found ({label}).
ev.noBlock: We could not find an overnight charging block in your data — type yours and we will price it.
ev.notReady: Tag a nightly kWh above to price the charge under all three plans.
ev.ofThat: Of that: {shift}/mo for moving the hour, {plan}/mo for changing plan at your hour. The two add up to the total and are never counted twice.
ev.peakExposureBody_one: {count} weekday afternoon hour sits in ULO's 16:00–21:00 peak window. Keep using it and a ULO switch makes it one of the most expensive hours you buy.
ev.peakExposureBody_other: {count} weekday afternoon hours sit in ULO's 16:00–21:00 peak window. Keep using them and a ULO switch makes them the most expensive hours you buy.
ev.perMonthMore: /mo more than the same energy overnight
ev.pickHour: Pick the hour your car draws the most power and we will price staying there against moving to midnight.
ev.priceAtHour: above — we will price staying at that hour on
ev.stayAtTitle: When do you charge? Stay at
ev.stayDetail: Priced from your own readings at {label}: {hours}.
ev.stayDetailUpper: No readings at {label}, so the stay side is priced at each plan's most expensive rate — an upper bound, not a measurement.

ev.worseOff: Staying at {label} on {plan} costs {stay}. Moving the same charge to 23:00–07:00 on Ultra-Low Overnight costs {move} — {delta} worse off every month. Don't move it.

gbseries.note.ambiguousInlineReadingType: An entry carried {count} inline ReadingTypes with no per-block link. Their readings were kept apart by ReadingType instead of merged, and none was converted, because which block belongs to which type is not stated.
gbseries.note.assumedDirection: Series {label} declares no usable flowDirection, so its readings were treated as delivered (forward) — the ESPI default for an interval feed.
gbseries.note.combinedConsumptionSeries: UsagePoint {point} carries {count} separate consumption series ({labels}). Their readings are combined in this group; every series is listed separately on the point so a picker or diagnostics panel can tell them apart.
gbseries.note.combinedDuplicateResolutio: UsagePoint {point} carries {count} consumption series that describe overlapping periods ({labels}). They repeat the same consumption at different sizes, so summing them would price the same energy more than once; only the finest series ({keeper}) was priced, and the {refused} reading(s) of the others that fall inside its coverage were refused.

UsagePoint {point} carries {count} consumption series that describe overlapping periods ({labels}). They repeat the same consumption at different sizes, so summing them would price the same energy more than once; only the finest series ({keeper}) was priced, and the {refused} reading(s) of the others that fall inside its coverage were refused. The {kept} reading(s) of theirs that lie outside that coverage were still priced.
gbseries.note.combinedEnergyAndPower: UsagePoint {point} publishes both per-interval energy ({energy}) and interval-average power ({power}). They describe the same consumption, so only the energy series was priced; the power series is preserved unconverted-to-total on the point.
gbseries.note.convertedToEnergy: Series {label} is interval-average real power ({uom}); each reading was converted to energy with its own interval duration.
gbseries.note.legacyAssumption: No ReadingType described {count} reading(s), so they were read as watt-hours scaled by the document-wide multiplier — the legacy compatibility path. The timestamps are exact; the unit is an assumption, not a declaration.
gbseries.note.legacyAssumptionNoUom: Series {label} declares no uom, so its values were read as watt-hours scaled by {multiplier} — the default for an interval energy feed, but an assumption rather than a declaration.
gbseries.note.refusedReadings: In series {label}, {negative} reading(s) failed value or direction validation, {unparsable} carried no usable start or value, and {magnitude} carried a magnitude no interval can hold (more than {max} kWh in one reading). None of them was priced; every count is recorded on the series.
gbseries.note.unlinkedReadingType: Series {label} carried no ReadingType link, so the document's only ReadingType ({uom}, {multiplier}) was applied. With one declared type in the document there is no other candidate to confuse it with, but this is a resolution, not a stated link.
gbseries.note.unsupportedSeries: Series {label} was NOT loaded as consumption: it {reason} Its readings are preserved here and none of them was priced.
gbseries.note.volumeSeries: Series {label} was loaded as volume: {count} reading(s) in {uom} scaled by {multiplier} — a quantity, not energy, so none of it was priced or added to the kWh totals.

gbseries.reasons: Why some of this point was left out:
gbseries.refusal.combinedFlow: combines directions (net, total or a quadrant), so it belongs to neither the import nor the export stream.
gbseries.refusal.otherCommodity: measures a non-electricity commodity (gas, water, steam, refuse …), so it must never be priced with electricity rates.
gbseries.refusal.otherQuantity: measures apparent or reactive energy or power, or a unit that is not an amount of energy at all.
gbseries.refusal.register: is a register reading (its ESPI accumulationBehaviour is a cumulative, bulk or summation quantity), not an interval increment: registers must be differenced against a known reset, and no such contract is available here.
gbseries.refusal.reverseFlow: is exported (received) energy — adding it to consumption would overstate usage.
gbseries.refusal.spot: is a spot measurement (indicating, instantaneous or time-delayed), so it has no interval it could be an amount of energy for.
gbseries.refusal.unconvertible: cannot be converted to energy with the metadata the feed provides.
gbseries.refusal.unresolvedReadingType: has no ReadingType that could be tied to it, although the document declares ReadingTypes for other series: its unit, scale and interval are unknown, so its values were kept but not converted.

policy.account.policyNotice: Review the current Privacy and Account Terms versions. Existing accounts are not silently migrated; this notice appears on account interaction until a current acknowledgement is recorded.
policy.notLegal: This product disclosure is not legal advice or a legal-compliance certification.
policy.privacy.encryptionBody: Usage backups are encrypted in your browser before upload. The service cannot decrypt them. The server stores only the encrypted blob and metadata needed to version and deliver it.
policy.privacy.intro: This page describes what the account service can receive and persist. Usage decisions and readings remain in your browser.
policy.privacy.logsBody: Source IP and user-agent operational logs follow the documented privacy-safe format. They are operational records, not usage readings or a readable copy of your encrypted backup.
policy.privacy.metadataBody: Server-side metadata includes your email, account creation, sign-in and session activity, encrypted-blob size, revision and update time, push-subscription and notification-preference metadata, and notification title, outcome and detail, subject to retention.
policy.privacy.notificationBody: A notification body may transit the push provider or this server so it can be delivered, but notification bodies must not persist. Notification titles, outcomes and details are the metadata recorded for delivery diagnostics.
policy.privacy.recoveryBody: Password or recovery-code loss may make an encrypted backup unrecoverable. Recovery can restore account access, but it cannot decrypt an old blob without an existing device or data key.
policy.privacy.retentionBody: The current concrete retention policy is not yet available. We do not claim unlimited retention, legal certification, or a multi-instance/high-availability service.
policy.privacy.title: Privacy
policy.registrationDisabled: The concrete retention policy is not yet available. Account registration stays disabled until that policy can be enforced.
policy.terms.acceptanceBody: Before a verified registration can become a usable account, you must leave this acknowledgement unchecked until you have read both this page and the Privacy page, then check it explicitly. The accepted Privacy and Account Terms versions and the acceptance timestamp are recorded with the account.
policy.terms.acknowledgement: I have read and acknowledge the Privacy and Account Terms pages.
policy.terms.availabilityBody: Registration is currently disabled because the concrete retention policy is not yet available for enforcement. The service makes no promise of unlimited retention, legal certification, or multi-instance/high availability.
policy.terms.intro: These account terms describe the product boundary for an optional account. They do not change the browser-first data model.
policy.terms.recoveryBody: A recovery code can restore access to an account. It cannot create a missing device or data key, and it cannot decrypt an old encrypted backup when no existing device or data key remains.
policy.terms.serviceBody: The account mirrors browser-encrypted data for multi-device sync. The service cannot read the usage readings inside that encrypted blob. Account sign-in, session, sync, push and notification metadata are handled as described in Privacy.
policy.terms.title: Account Terms
preflight.checklistTitle: What must be true before activation is even considered
preflight.detail.accountEnabled.pass: This deployment was told to be the account server: its account routes answer.
preflight.detail.accountEnabled.pending: The account feature is switched off, so every /account/ route answers 404 on purpose.
preflight.detail.emailVerification.pass: Mailbox ownership is proven before a password is chosen.
preflight.detail.emailVerification.pendi: Email verification is switched off, so registration cannot be opened.
preflight.detail.smtp.pass: The sender contract is complete: every SMTP field and credential mount this deployment needs is present.
preflight.detail.smtp.pending: SMTP is not provisioned. There is no sender contract, so no verification or recovery mail could be delivered.
preflight.failClosed: Account activation stays fail-closed until SMTP is live. Nothing is broken here: without working email delivery this deployment deliberately refuses to activate accounts, so the guard you are looking at is doing its job.
preflight.intro: A read-only check of what account activation needs before it can be considered.
preflight.item.1: SMTP is provisioned end to end — host, port, TLS mode, HELO, sender and reply-to on this domain, the credential file mounts and a timeout — so the sender contract config.ts requires is complete.
preflight.item.2: A real message has been delivered to a real mailbox and read there. Configuration alone is not proof that email works.
preflight.item.3: ACCT_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_ENABLED is explicitly true, so mailbox ownership is proven before anyone chooses a password.
preflight.item.4: ACCT_ENABLED is explicitly true on the account container, with the data directory mounted outside the repository and mode-checked, so the account process can boot.
preflight.item.5: The published retention policy is concrete enough to enforce — registration stays disabled until it is.
preflight.item.6: A written rollback: who flips the two flags back, and what happens to any account created in the meantime.
preflight.item.7: Explicit, recorded authorization to activate — a separate decision that this page neither makes nor grants.
preflight.readOnly: Read-only: this page reads configuration and changes no flag, no SMTP setting, no credential and no account.
preflight.readyNote: Every prerequisite this page can read is satisfied. Activation is still a separate, explicit decision — this page neither makes it nor grants it.
preflight.title: Account activation preflight
